meta.note: Specs and terms are transcribed from vendor official pages; fields not stated on official pages read “Check the official page”. group values: free (free tier). status values: active (free tier). cardRequired null means the official page does not state it; false means the official site states no credit card is required. planKind has the same meaning as group, with the value free-tier (free tier). planName is the vendor plan name. specText summarizes the free allowances in the official wording; durationText covers duration and permanence; cardNote covers card requirements; limitsText covers key limits; risks covers notes; flags are entry feature markers: public-only (some features in the comparison table are limited to public repositories), no-card-signup (sign-up needs no credit card), shared-runner-card (shared runners require card verification), user-limit (per-group user limit), unlimited-repos (no repository count limit). New markers: foss-only (free/libre software projects only), private-limit (private content has a size cap). overageBehavior states the overage behavior from the official page (present on entries added 2026-11-14); fields not stated read “Check the official page”.

offers.title: GitHub Free
offers.specText: Unlimited public/private repositories; Dependabot; 2,000 CI/CD minutes/month; 500 MB Packages storage; Issues & Projects; community support; Codespaces access ($0 spend limit)
offers.durationText: Free (the official pages read do not state permanent wording)
offers.cardNote: Not stated on the official pages read — check the official page.
offers.limitsText: Several features in the comparison table are limited to public repositories (repository rules, code owners, draft PRs, Pages/wikis, secret scanning, and others); Codespaces free hours go only to personal accounts, not to free organizations; pricing page example: 2-core machines 60 hours, 4-core machines 30 hours
risks: Several features in the comparison table are limited to public repositories and unavailable for private repositories
Codespaces free hours go only to personal accounts, not to free organizations
Card requirements are not stated on the official pages read — check the official page
offers.notes: Public repository Actions minutes and Packages are free; Team $4/user/month (3,000 minutes, 2 GB); Enterprise $21/user/month (50,000 minutes, 50 GB).

offers.title: GitLab Free
offers.specText: 5 users per top-level group; 400 compute minutes/month; 10 GiB adjustable storage; 5 GiB data transfer per month
offers.durationText: Free; the pricing page states "No credit card required"
offers.cardNote: Sign-up needs no credit card (pricing page wording: "No credit card required"); using shared runners requires card verification ($1 authorization check, no charge), while a bring-your-own runner or disabling shared runners needs no card.
offers.limitsText: 5 users per top-level group; 400 compute minutes/month; 10 GiB adjustable storage; 5 GiB data transfer per month
risks: Shared runners require card verification ($1 authorization check, no charge)
offers.notes: Premium $29/user/month (annual billing); Ultimate has no public price, and the pricing page writes "Contact us for custom pricing" (quote-based pricing).

offers.title: Bitbucket Free
offers.specText: Up to 5 users; unlimited public/private repositories; 50 build minutes per month; 1 GB LFS file storage (plus 1 GB storage per repository); build minutes and storage shared by all users in the workspace
offers.durationText: Free (the official pages read do not state permanent wording)
offers.cardNote: Free-tier card requirements are not stated on the official pages read — check the official page.
offers.limitsText: Up to 5 users; 50 build minutes per month; 1 GB LFS file storage (the documentation page states 1 GB large file storage in total); build minutes scale by runner size (a 5-minute step on a 2x runner counts as 10 minutes)
offers.overageBehavior: The documentation page states no overage protection on the Free plan (Overage protection: Not included); the pricing page states 1,000 more minutes or 100 GB for $10 per month.
risks: Up to 5 users; build minutes and storage are shared by all users in the workspace
50 build minutes per month, scaled by runner size
Free-tier card requirements are not stated on the official pages read — check the official page
Paid plan prices differ between the pricing page and the documentation page; see the detail page
offers.notes: Pricing page: Standard $3.65/user/month, Premium $8/user/month; documentation limitations page: Standard $3/user/month ($15/month for 1-5 users), Premium $6/user/month ($30/month for 1-5 users), both wordings presented side by side. Documentation page: Standard 2,500 build minutes per month, Premium 3,500 build minutes per month. Community/academic subscriptions (eligibility-based): unlimited private repositories and contributors, 5 GB LFS storage, 500 build minutes.

offers.title: Codeberg free hosting
offers.specText: Free hosting for free/libre software projects (Forgejo); public repositories need a suitable license; 100 repositories per user/organization by default; requests needed above 750 MiB Git storage and 1.5 GiB packages/LFS/attachments; private content capped at 100 MB (for free software contributors); Forgejo Actions default runners need no request, Woodpecker CI access is granted per account
offers.durationText: Free; the FAQ states no payment is required for any service, and membership is fully optional
offers.cardNote: The FAQ states no payment is required for any service, and association membership is fully optional.
offers.limitsText: Free/libre software projects only; public repositories need a suitable license; no private hosting services; private content capped at 100 MB (the requests page states 100 MiB per user); 100 repositories by default; requests needed above 750 MiB Git storage or 1.5 GiB packages/LFS/attachments; Woodpecker CI access is granted per account
offers.overageBehavior: No quota for valid use cases; requests are needed before exceeding default resources — check the official page.
risks: Free/libre software projects only; public repositories need a suitable license
No private hosting services; commercial private repositories are pointed to self-hosted Forgejo
Private content is capped at 100 MB, for free software contributors
Woodpecker CI access is granted per account; monthly CI minute figures are not stated on the official pages read
offers.notes: No paid plans; funded by donations and membership fees. The FAQ states 100 MB of private content; the requests page states 100 MiB per user; both unit wordings are presented side by side.

offers.title: Azure DevOps free allowances
offers.specText: First 5 Basic users free; unlimited private Git repositories; 1 Microsoft-hosted parallel job with 1,800 minutes per month; 1 self-hosted parallel job with unlimited minutes; 2 GiB of Artifacts free per organization; Boards and the Pipelines free offer included with Basic
offers.durationText: Free (the official pages read do not state permanent wording); free build amounts reset on the first day of the month
offers.cardNote: The pricing page FAQ states a credit card is not necessary to get started; a card is set up in the purchase experience when more services or more users are added.
offers.limitsText: First 5 Basic users free, $6/user/month from the 6th user; further users default to the Stakeholder tier, and Basic licenses are needed for access to Repos/Boards; Microsoft-hosted jobs allow 1,800 minutes per month
offers.overageBehavior: Free build amounts reset on the first day of the month; extra parallel jobs cost $40/Microsoft-hosted and $15/self-hosted per month; Artifacts beyond 2 GiB use tiered pricing.
risks: Users beyond the first 5 default to the Stakeholder tier; Basic licenses are needed for access to Repos/Boards
The pricing page notes that prices are estimates — check the official page
Microsoft-hosted jobs allow 1,800 minutes per month; self-hosted job minutes are unlimited, with machines supplied separately
offers.notes: Basic + Test Plans $52/user/month. Unlimited users can access Pipelines and Artifacts at no extra charge. Visual Studio subscribers get free access and do not count against the 5 free users (pricing page).
